editorial.headline: Industrial Colour, Ink and Coating Preparations, Kept Open
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20229 covers the making of pigment, dye, ink and coating preparations, with national foreign ownership open and no Bali PMA block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20229 is an industrial manufacturing code for prepared colour and surface materials. The Indonesian scope places it around the making of pigment preparations and dye materials, colourants and opacifiers where the maker is not otherwise specified, polishing enamels and coating preparations, printing ink, artists' paints and other coating materials. In practical terms, this is not the retail sale of paint or the application of coatings on a building; it is the production side of formulated colour, ink and coating preparations themselves.

The record opens this activity across the full scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the code is not reserved only for a narrow industrial tier in the slim record. A small manufacturer preparing specialised coating materials and a larger producer working at industrial scale are both inside the scale envelope, provided the activity being registered remains the making of these preparations. The scope is broad, but it is still disciplined: pigment preparations, dye materials, opacifiers, enamels, printing inks, artists' paints and other coatings are the centre of gravity.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA and the maximum foreign ownership recorded is 100%. There is no partial cap to interpret, no lower foreign ceiling to explain, and no extra percentage hidden in the text. The national source given for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the face of this slim record, a foreign-owned company can treat the activity as nationally open rather than nationally restricted.

Bali does not change that conclusion into a block. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says the activity is not blocked for PMA in Bali. The reason is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA in Bali, island-wide and permanently; this record says KBLI 20229 does not fall into that blocked outcome. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally open, foreign ownership up to 100%, and not blocked for Bali PMA registration in the slim record.
